request.spec:
A bulk settle is now all-or-nothing: if any selected claim cannot be settled by the signed-in
user (any refusal the single settle would give; going to PENDING is not a refusal), none of them is
settled, every one counts as refused and nothing is written. Otherwise every selected claim is
settled in list order as before, and after the claims' own lines one line BATCH_SETTLED
batch=<batch number> count=<claims in the batch> total=<the frozen figures of those SETTLED, added
up> is written.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A bulk settle is now all-or-nothing: if any selected claim cannot be settled by the signed-in
user (any refusal the single settle would give; going to PENDING is not a refusal), none of them is
settled, every one counts as refused and nothing is written. Otherwise every selected claim is
settled in list order as before, and after the claims' own lines one line BATCH_SETTLED
batch=<batch number> count=<claims in the batch> total=<the frozen figures of those SETTLED, added
up> is written.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Bulk settle is now all-or-nothing, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the acceptance spec.

**What it does now:**
- **Check first:** before anything is settled, each selected claim goes through the same checks a single settle would make. These checks write nothing. If any claim would be refused, or isn't on the sheet, the request settles nothing, writes nothing to the store or the audit file, and reports every selected claim as refused. A claim that would go to PENDING doesn't count as refused.
- **Otherwise:** every claim is settled in list order as before, with the same per-claim audit lines. After them comes one `BATCH_SETTLED sheet=… by=… batch=<n> count=<claims in batch> total=<sum>` line. The total adds up the frozen figures of the claims that ended up SETTLED only. A claim made PENDING counts toward `count` but not `total`, and if nothing reached SETTLED the total is `0.00`.

The change is in `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/claim/SettleClaims.java`, and I updated the description comment in `bulk-settle.POST.yml` to match. The front end didn't need any change.

**One gap:** the all-or-nothing guarantee rests on the up-front check. If someone else changes one of the claims between that check and the save, that claim is skipped and counted refused while the others still settle, as before. Covering that would mean undoing database changes and audit lines that were already made. I didn't do that, and no test hits it.

probe.probe_text:
I made no changes. Everything below comes from reading the Java back end (`src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/**`) and the React front end (`src/main/frontend/features/**`). **One thing first:** the server does not send the screen any computed figures. It sends raw claims, people, rates and settings. The front end works out every due, total, overdue and age figure itself, mainly in `features/rates/rates.ts`, `overdue/late.ts`, `claims/claims.ts` and `periods/periods.ts`. The back end works out the same rules a second time, in `claim/ClaimDue.java`, `LateCharge.java`, `Rounding.java`, `rollup/Rollup.java`, `period/ClosePeriod.java` and `statement/TakeStatement.java`. It uses its copy to freeze figures, to check limits and thresholds, and to write the audit file. So each rule below normally lives in two places. ## 1. Figures and the rules behind them ### Per claim (`claim-*`, rendered in `claims.slot.tsx` `ClaimRow`) | Figure | Rule | |---|---| | `claim-number` | Given when the claim is opened (`ClaimNumbering.next`). Normally it is the sheet-wide next number (1, 2, …). When `period-numbering-from` is set and the sheet's today is on or after it (`perPeriod`), the number is `-` for the period that contains the claim's **due-by**, or `X-` if no period does. A voided claim keeps its number, and a rolled-back open gives its number back. | | `claim-amount`, `claim-date`, `claim-note`, `claim-ref`, `claim-tags` | **Amount:** up to two decimals. It may be negative only for a correction (`Corrections.check`), which must name a SETTLED claim of the same person. **Date:** if left blank it is `settings.claimDate`, meaning the `entry-date` setting if set, else the sheet's today. **Ref:** must be unique on the sheet, case ignored (`ClaimRules.checkRef`). **Tags:** trimmed, lower-cased, de-duplicated, sorted (`ClaimValues.tags`). | | `claim-due` | The front end's `claimDue` and the back end's `ClaimDue.figure` + `LateCharge.add`, in this order:
1. If the claim has a frozen `due` (set at settle), show that.
2. Else, if it is `bound` (`stated` and not PENDING), use `statedDue`.
3. Else use the live figure `ClaimDue.live`: amount × the rate in force on the claim's date, for the person's grade on that date (`gradeOn`), rounded to 2 dp. `n/a` if no rate applies (`RateRepository.find` also honours the rate's to-date).
4. Add the **late charge** (`LateCharge.on` / `lateBoundaries`). For every full 30 days past `lateFrom`, the claim gains the `late-pct` in force on that boundary date, compounding on figure + earlier charges, each step rounded. There is no charge for a frozen due, a correction, a deferred claim, or a claim that is not OPEN/PENDING.
5. Apply the **floor** last: at least the `floor` in force on the claim's date (default 1.00). There is no floor for a correction or a frozen due. | | Rounding | `Rounding.mode` / `roundsHalfUp`. A claim whose `roundsOn` date is before `policy-date` rounds HALF_UP; otherwise HALF_EVEN. If `policy-date` is blank, the sheet's today is used instead. `roundsOn` is the corrected claim's date for a correction, else the claim's own date. | | `claim-due-by` | Fixed when the claim is added (`ClaimRules.dueBy`): the `terms`-th business day after its date, skipping weekends and sheet holidays (`HolidayRepository.businessDaysAfter`). The terms are the person's own terms, else `terms-` for their grade on that date, else `terms` (default 14). The claim keeps the terms it was fixed with. Adding a holiday re-fixes the due-by of every claim that is not SETTLED/VOID and whose due-by is on or after the holiday (`refixDueBys`). Re-dating leaves the due-by, number and period alone. | | `claim-overdue` | `isOverdue`: the claim is OPEN or PENDING, not deferred, and `lateFrom` is before today. `lateFrom` = due-by + `grace-` (grade on the claim's date, grace in force on that date). | | `claim-status` | DRAFT → OPEN → SETTLED, with PENDING and VOID branches. Full rules are in the section on who may do what. | | `claim-opened-by` | Set when the claim is opened. | | `claim-stated` | `stated`: the person's last statement bound this claim. | | `claim-corrects` | Number of the claim this correction corrects. | | `claim-deferred`, `claim-deferred-until` | `ClaimDue.deferred`: an OPEN claim whose `deferredUntil` is after today. While deferred it counts in no total, is not overdue, cannot be settled or split, and is not bound by a statement. Only an OPEN claim can be deferred, and only to a date after today. | | `claim-proofs` | A counter. Proofs can't be added to SETTLED/VOID claims or to a claim whose due-by is in a closed period. | | `claim-split-from` | The number of the claim this one was split from. A split works only on an OPEN, not-deferred claim, for 0 < amount < its amount, by a role allowed to open. The original loses its statement binding. | | `claim-late-entry` | The claim was added while its due-by's period was **soft-closed**. | | `claim-reminded` | The last reminder date. One reminder per sheet-today, OPEN/PENDING claims only. | | `claim-batch` | The bulk-settle batch number. A later single settle clears it. | | `claim-period` | `periodOf(periods, c.dueBy)`: the period containing the **due-by**, not the claim's date. | | `claim-log-line` | One line per status change: ` by on due=` (`ClaimLog`). | ### Per person (`PersonRow` slot contributions) Several of these figures start from the same filter, `live()` in the front end (`ClaimDue.countsLive` in the back end). A claim passes when it **counts**: it is OPEN, PENDING or SETTLED, and not deferred. It is still left out if it is OPEN/PENDING, **not bound** by a statement, and either dated inside one of the person's **holds** (`heldOn`) or the person's retirement date is on or before today (`retiredOn`). | Figure | Rule | |---|---| | `person-claimed` | The sum of the amounts of the live claims (`total(live(...))`). | | `person-due-total` | `personDue`: the sum of the live claims' `claimDue`, held to the `cap` in force today (`SettingRepository.capped`). It is `n/a` when the person's grade today has no rate **and** no counting claim has a figure. | | `person-excess` | How far that sum is above the cap, else 0.00. | | `person-settled-total` / `person-open-total` | `personSplit`: the same figures, split by SETTLED vs OPEN/PENDING. Not capped. | | `person-overdue-count` / `person-overdue-total` | The count of live claims that are overdue, and the sum of their dues (late charge included). Not capped. | | `person-aged-0-30` / `31-60` / `61` | `aged`: dues of live OPEN/PENDING, not-deferred claims, bucketed by days from the claim's **date** to today. A claim dated in the future goes in 0-30. | | `person-active` | `isActive`: has a live OPEN/PENDING claim dated in the 30 days up to and including today. | | `person-period--due-total` | `personPeriodDue`: claims whose **due-by** falls in the period and that counted by the status they had at the end of the period's last day (`statusAsOf` on the status log). The hold, retirement and binding exclusions use the claim's status *now*. For a closed or soft-closed period, the value is the per-person figure frozen at close (`personTotals`), or 0.00 for someone added later. | | `person-statement-count`, `person-stated-total`, `person-statement-date` | `TakeStatement` records the person's due-total at that moment (capped, `n/a` rule as above) and binds every counting claim to its **rate figure** at that moment, without floor or late charge (those keep following today). Claims that don't count are unbound. A statement can be taken "as of" a date that is on or before today and not before the person was added; it then uses the sheet as it stood (`SheetAsOf`). Only a steward cancels a statement. Cancelling unbinds the claims; an earlier statement's binding is not restored. | | `person-backing` | Sum of the frozen dues of the person's **patrons'** SETTLED claims dated within the 90 days up to and including today. | | `person-grade` | Grade in force on today. Grades are dated: an edit records a grade from a from-date (blank = today). Bulk grade goes through the same steps. | | `person-terms` | The person's own terms. | | `person-retired` / `person-retired-from` | A person counts as retired as soon as a retirement date is set, whatever the date. No claim of theirs may be dated after it (`mayClaimOn`). Their claims leave the live totals once today reaches it. | | `person-hold-line` | Holds run from a date (blank = today) to an optional end date. | | `person-watched` | Whether the signed-in user watches the person. A settle, approve or re-settle writes NOTIFY lines to the audit file. | ### Sheet-wide - **`rollup-claimed-total`:** everyone's claimed, added up. - **`rollup-due-total` / `header-due-total`:** `trimmedSum` of the people's due-totals. `n/a` values are skipped, and with three or more values the single highest and the single lowest are dropped. - **`rollup-overdue-total` / `header-overdue-total`:** trimmed the same way. **`rollup-overdue-count`** is a plain sum. - **`rollup-settled-total` / `rollup-open-total`:** plain sums, not trimmed. - **`month--due-total`:** live claims grouped by the month of their **date**. - **`tag--due-total`:** live claims carrying the tag. A claim with two tags counts in both. - **`period-due-total` / `summary-period-*`:** the sum of the per-person period figures, or the total frozen at close or soft-close. - **`summary-grade--count`, `-due-total`, `-active`:** people on that grade today, **retired people excluded**, with their summed due-totals and how many are active. - **`header-people-count`:** **retired people included**, unlike the summary. - **`summary-status-*` / `header-claims-*-count`:** claim counts per status. - **`summary-void-*`:** claim counts per void reason. - **`rate-current-`:** the rate in force today. - **`rate-preview-count` / `rate-preview-diff`:** OPEN/PENDING claims on that grade whose due would change under a candidate rate. Bound claims don't change. Nothing is saved. ### Who may do what (`ApplyClaimStatus`, `SettingRepository.permits`, `RoleRepository`, `ViewerGuard`) **Roles** - Roles are clerk (the default for any name), steward and viewer. - A **delegation** makes a user a steward while the sheet's today is inside its date range. Only a steward who holds the role directly (not by delegation) can delegate. - **Viewers, archived sheets and as-of screens** can't change anything: the request is refused with 403. Bulk actions instead report 0 done. **Permissions** - `perm-open`, `perm-settle`, `perm-void`, `perm-reassign`, `perm-close` and `perm-reopen` each list the roles allowed to take that action. - When one is blank, the default is: open, settle, void and close by clerk or steward; reassign and reopen by steward only. **Status changes** - **Edit:** only a DRAFT can be edited. The editor locks the claim to its user; a change of the sheet's today releases all locks. - **Open:** DRAFT → OPEN. It is refused when the note is empty and the due as shown is above the `note-threshold` in force on the claim's date. - **Settle:** - **Four eyes:** neither the user who opened the claim nor its last editor may settle or approve it. - **Proofs:** with 0 proofs, it is refused when the due is above the proof threshold. The threshold is `proof-threshold-`, else `proof-threshold`, in force on the claim's date. This is checked before the clerk limit. - **Clerk limit:** a non-steward settling above `clerk-limit` makes the claim PENDING, with its due still live. - **What settling freezes:** the due as shown — the figure (or the bound figure), plus the late charge as of today, at least the floor. - **Approve or reject:** steward only, on a PENDING claim. A rejection needs a reason. - **Void:** - DRAFT, OPEN or PENDING claims can be voided. A SETTLED claim can be voided only by a steward, within `VOID_SETTLED_DAYS = 7` of its settle date in the log. - While the sheet has a void-reason list, a reason from that list is required. - A VOID claim leaves every total. - **Re-settle:** steward only. The due is frozen again at today's figure for the claim as if OPEN and not bound. - **Re-date:** steward only, OPEN/PENDING claims. Refused if the new date is after the person's retirement. - **Reassign (move):** DRAFT, OPEN or PENDING claims; not a correction; not to the claim's own person or a person who retired before the claim's date. - **Bulk actions:** - **Bulk settle:** all or nothing, and it creates a BATCH. - **Bulk open and bulk reassign:** each claim on its own; a claim that fails is counted as refused. ### What a closed period changes - **Closed:** `PeriodRepository.closedOn(dueBy)`. A claim whose **due-by** is inside a closed period cannot be added, edited, locked, opened, settled, voided, deferred, given a proof, split, re-dated or moved. Its figures are frozen. - **Soft-closed:** the figures are frozen the same way, but claims can still change. A claim added during a soft close is flagged `lateEntry`. - **Reopen:** governed by the reopen permission, a steward while it is blank. - **Auto-close:** when the sheet's today changes, every open period whose to-date + `grace-days` is before the new today is closed (`AutoClosePeriods`). - **New and generated periods:** a new period's name must be unique and it may not overlap another period. Generated periods are monthly, named yyyy-mm, and skip names or days already taken. ### What a date decides The **sheet's today**, never the real clock (`SheetRepository.today`), drives: - overdue status, the late charge, the cap, the default policy date, the default claim date, grade-today and rate-today - holds and retirement cut-offs, deferral and active status - aging, backing, the 7-day void window, reminders and auto-close Most settings are **dated**: they have a from-date and the value in force on the relevant date applies. That date is the claim's date for floor, grace, note and proof thresholds; each 30-day boundary for `late-pct`; and today for cap and clerk limit. `policy-date`, `period-numbering-from`, `entry-date`, `grace-days` and the permission settings are undated. **As-of view** (`AsOf`, `SheetAsOf`, `RespondWithClaims.asItStood`): every read shows what was stored while the sheet's today was on or before the chosen date, with that date standing in for today. A claim's status comes from its log, and its values from before any later edit. It is bound only if the statement had been taken by then. Every change is refused while the view is set. ### Imports and quick-add - **Paste** (`ValidatePasteClaims`, `CheckPastedClaims`): - Each line is `name,amount,date,note`; a trailing ` #ref` in the note becomes the claim's reference. - Every line must keep the rules for adding a claim, and refs may not repeat across lines. - It is all or nothing: one bad line refuses the whole paste. - Claims are added as DRAFTs in paste order. - **Quick-add:** adds a DRAFT with the default date and an empty note. An unknown name creates a grade-A person first; the closed-period check runs before that person is created. ### Audit-only effects `ROLLUP` and `TOTALS` lines are written when a person's figures (claimed, due-total, overdue-total) or the sheet's totals move. ## 2. How hard it was to follow It was hard. The rules aren't in one place. Each one is split across about 117 claim classes in small one-method pipeline steps, plus YAML wiring and repository SQL. On top of that, every figure is worked out twice: once in Java for freezing, checks and the audit file, and again in TypeScript for what the screen shows. The long Javadoc comments are the only map, and they have already drifted in places — for example, the front-end `periods.ts` comment says "dated inside" a closed period while the code checks the due-by. A new developer would have to follow `ClaimDue`, `LateCharge`, `Rounding`, `Rollup`, `rates.ts` and `late.ts` side by side and keep both copies in step by hand.
